lessons.title: Compressible Flow: Preliminary Aspects
lessons.summary: The thermodynamics of a calorically perfect gas, the first and second laws, entropy and the isentropic relations, compressibility and when a flow must be treated as compressible, the governing equations, and total (stagnation) conditions.
lessons.description: Interactive lesson on the preliminaries of compressible flow: perfect-gas thermodynamics, the first and second laws, entropy and isentropic relations on a T-s diagram, compressibility, the governing equations for inviscid compressible flow, and total conditions, with why Bernoulli's equation fails at high speed. MAE 3293, Oklahoma State University.
lessons.image_alt: Total-to-static pressure ratio versus Mach number from the isentropic relation and from Bernoulli's equation, with the total enthalpy split into static enthalpy and kinetic energy

lessons.title: Normal Shock Waves
lessons.summary: The speed of sound, total and sonic reference conditions, and the characteristic Mach number; the normal-shock relations, the entropy rise and total-pressure loss across a shock, and the Pitot tube in subsonic and supersonic flow.
lessons.description: Interactive lesson on normal shock waves: the speed of sound, total and sonic conditions, the characteristic Mach number, the normal-shock relations and Prandtl relation, entropy and total-pressure loss across a shock, and Pitot-tube measurements in subsonic and supersonic flow. MAE 3293, Oklahoma State University.
lessons.image_alt: Normal-shock property ratios versus upstream Mach number, with a stationary normal shock and the velocities ahead of and behind it

lessons.title: Oblique Shock and Expansion Waves
lessons.summary: Mach waves, the θ–β–M relation, shock reflection, Prandtl–Meyer expansion and isentropic compression, and shock-expansion theory for flat-plate, wedge, and diamond airfoils.
lessons.description: Interactive lesson on oblique shocks, Mach waves, the θ–β–M relation, shock reflection, Prandtl–Meyer expansion and isentropic compression, and shock-expansion theory for flat-plate, wedge and diamond airfoils. MAE 3293, Oklahoma State University.
lessons.image_alt: Diamond airfoil in supersonic flow with oblique shocks, expansion fans and surface pressure arrows

lessons.title: Nozzles, Diffusers, and Wind Tunnels
lessons.summary: Quasi-one-dimensional flow: the area–velocity and area–Mach relations, choked flow, converging-diverging nozzles with normal shocks inside or at the exit, rocket thrust, diffusers, and supersonic wind-tunnel start-up.
lessons.description: Interactive lesson on quasi-one-dimensional compressible flow: the area–velocity and area–Mach relations, choked flow, converging-diverging nozzles with normal shocks inside or at the exit, overexpanded and underexpanded jets, rocket thrust, diffusers, and supersonic wind tunnels. MAE 3293, Oklahoma State University.
lessons.image_alt: Converging-diverging nozzle with a normal shock in the diverging section, with the pressure and Mach number distributions along the nozzle

calculators.title: Isentropic Flow
calculators.summary: Mach number, the total-to-static ratios p<sub>0</sub>/p, ρ<sub>0</sub>/ρ and T<sub>0</sub>/T, and the area ratio A/A*, from any one of them (Appendix A).
calculators.description: Isentropic-flow calculator for a calorically perfect gas: enter the Mach number, a total-to-static pressure, density or temperature ratio, or the area ratio A/A* (subsonic or supersonic branch) and read the rest, in place of Anderson's Appendix A. MAE 3293, Oklahoma State University.
calculators.image_alt: Isentropic-flow ratios p/p0, rho/rho0, T/T0 and A*/A versus Mach number, with the selected Mach number marked
lessons: Chapter 8, special forms of the energy equation

calculators.title: Normal Shock
calculators.summary: Downstream Mach number and the pressure, density, temperature and total-pressure ratios across a normal shock, including the Pitot ratio (Appendix B).

calculators.title: Oblique Shock
calculators.summary: The θ–β–M relation: any two of Mach number, deflection angle and wave angle give the third, with the property ratios across the shock.

calculators.title: Prandtl–Meyer Expansion
calculators.summary: Prandtl–Meyer function, Mach angle, and the flow downstream of an expansion fan turning through a given angle (Appendix C).

calculators.title: Supersonic Airfoils
calculators.summary: Shock-expansion theory for flat-plate, wedge and diamond airfoils, compared with linear theory: surface pressures, lift, wave drag and moment.
